issues.t: Roadster rear window comes unglued and falls out
issues.sym: On the convertible, the plastic-framed rear glass rattles, flaps or comes loose from the soft top. It can fall out while driving or while the top is moving, and rain can then get into the trunk and cabin.
issues.why: The rear glass is bonded to the fabric top with adhesive that weakens with age and heat. Most failures show up after the 3-year/36,000-mile warranty.
issues.next: If the glass starts to separate, keep the top up and stop using it, and avoid highway speeds. Get the window rebonded or the top replaced before it lets go. Ask a dealer whether any goodwill coverage still applies.

issues.sym: The engine suddenly shuts off at speed, sometimes with no warning light. Steering gets heavy. It may restart after a few minutes or not until it cools down.
issues.why: Failing crankshaft or camshaft position sensors are the most common finds. Some owners also traced it to the relay control module or ignition parts, and some cases were never diagnosed.
issues.next: Get to the side of the road safely. Have the crank and cam sensors and their wiring tested first, since they are the most common cause and fairly simple to replace.

issues.t: Relay control module failure causes stalling or no-start
issues.sym: The car won't crank or stalls, while the dash lights and radio still work. The problem comes and goes.
issues.why: The relay control module, which powers the engine circuits, can fail inside; owners blame weak solder joints and relays.
issues.next: Ask the shop to test the relay control module when the car won't start or stalls with no sensor codes.

issues.t: Key won't turn or sticks in the ignition
issues.sym: The key is hard to turn, gets stuck, or won't turn at all. Sometimes the car only starts after jiggling the key or turning the steering wheel.
issues.why: The ignition switch and lock housing wear, and the steering lock can bind.
issues.next: Don't force the key. Try turning the wheel gently while turning the key. Have the ignition switch and lock assembly replaced if it keeps happening.

issues.t: Anti-theft module failure stops the car from starting
issues.sym: The alarm sounds at random, or the car won't start because the anti-theft system doesn't recognize the key.
issues.why: The SKREEM module that controls the immobilizer, key and alarm can fail. A replacement must be programmed by a dealer.
issues.next: Note any security light or alarm behavior and go to a dealer or a shop with Chrysler programming tools.

issues.t: Alternator overcharges and ruins the battery
issues.sym: A rotten-egg smell, electrical problems and warning lights, and possibly the engine dying on the highway.
issues.why: A failed voltage regulator in the alternator pushes too much voltage, boiling the battery and stressing other electronics.
issues.next: If you smell sulfur, have the charging voltage checked right away. Replace the alternator and battery together.

issues.t: Convertible top stops working or drops on its own
issues.sym: The power top won't go up or down, or it falls open while parked or driving.
issues.why: The power top system fails; one dealer blamed water getting in at the rear of the top.
issues.next: Keep the top up and latched until it is repaired. Have the top motor, hydraulics, switches and seals checked.

issues.sym: One or both heated seats stay cold even though the switch light comes on.
issues.why: The heating element in the seat breaks, which is the most reported Crossfire problem on RepairPal. Chrysler offers repair kits.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or upholstery shop about the seat heater repair kit instead of a whole new seat pad.

issues.t: Brake lights stop working with a brake assist warning
issues.sym: The brake assist (BAS) warning light comes on when you brake, and the brake lights quit working.
issues.why: The brake light switch also feeds the brake assist system, so a fault there disables both.
issues.next: Have someone confirm your brake lights work. Get the brake light switch and its circuit checked soon, since other drivers can't see you stopping.

issues.t: Airbag light from a faulty clock spring
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on.
issues.why: The clock spring, the coiled wire in the steering column that connects the driver airbag, and the steering angle sensor can fail.
issues.next: An airbag light means the airbags may not work. Have the system scanned and repaired.

issues.t: Takata driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall 16V-081)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom. You may get a recall letter.
issues.why: The driver front airbag inflator can break apart in a crash and send metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the free replacement at a dealer as soon as possible.

issues.t: A/C and heater blower cuts out or stops
issues.sym: The fan fades in and out or stops, so neither the A/C nor heater blows air.
issues.why: Dealers have pointed to failed blower-related sensors or the blower motor; the cause isn't always clear.
issues.next: Have the blower motor, its control and wiring tested before replacing larger A/C parts.

issues.sym: Coolant leaks from the front of the car and the temperature may climb.
issues.next: Don't keep driving if it overheats. Replace the radiator and check hoses at the same time.

issues.t: Turn signal quits from a shorting bulb socket
issues.sym: A turn signal stops working, then may work again, and the problem returns.
issues.why: A worn spot in the bulb holder lets it short out. Replacing the whole headlight didn't always fix it.
issues.next: Inspect the bulb and socket for damage before buying a full headlight unit.

issues.sym: Exterior light bulbs keep burning out and need frequent replacing.
issues.why: The cause isn't clear from owner reports; a loose socket or voltage problem can shorten bulb life.
issues.next: If bulbs fail often, have the sockets and charging voltage checked.

issues.t: Rear sway bar brackets break loose
issues.sym: A squeak from the rear that turns into a clunk over bumps.
issues.why: The brackets that hold the rear sway bar to the body rust or crack apart.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension mounts inspected. New brackets usually need to be welded in by a body shop.
